4af0c6ab01e72c785d25762bcae6409e:
United States casino magnate Sheldon Adelson provided Guatemala’s official delegation a Boeing 767 to travel to Israel for the relocation of its embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
Guatemalan foreign minister Sandra Jovel said Adelson provided the plane last week to carry government officials and guests, including religious leaders.
Manfredo Marroquin, director of civil society organization Citizen Action, said President Jimmy Morales’s administration violated Guatemalan law, which forbids accepting such gifts.
Guatemala’s human rights prosecutor, Jordan Rodas, also said the arrangement with Adelson was concerning.
Morales’s decision to move Guatemala’s embassy just two days after the US did the same was seen by many as an attempt to curry favor with US President Donald Trump.
fd411979d5ee2111f772f0aa95e7c440:
An Alexandria military court issued preliminary death sentences against 36 people convicted of involvement in deadly bombings on two Egyptian churches in Alexandria and Tanta in April 2017.
The case involves 48 defendants, 31 of whom are in custody and 17 are fugitives.
The court has referred the case to the country's Grand Mufti for his non-binding opinion on the death sentence as per Egyptian law.
The verdict is subject to appeal.
The defendants were convicted of a number of terrorist attacks against civilians and policemen in 2016 and 2017.
In April 2017, suicide bombers attacked St George's Church in Tanta and St Mark's Cathedral in Alexandria on Palm Sunday, killing 46 people and injuring dozens.
The defendants were also charged with participating in a January 2017 attack on a security checkpoint in Egypt’s New Valley governorate near the Western Desert, killing eight policemen.
ac1824df8ffb507219a0310f9b796252:
Egypt’s Court of Cassation overturned death sentences and jail terms and ordered a retrial for defendants previously convicted in the “Waraq terrorist cell” case.
The court ordered the retrial after reviewing appeals filed by eight of the defendants, who had been sentenced to verdicts ranging from five-year prison terms, life imprisonment and death sentences.
The defendants will be retried in a different criminal court district.
A Giza criminal court sentenced two of the defendants to death, two to life imprisonment, and four to five-year terms in 2021.
The defendants were convicted of joining an outlawed group, killing a policeman and a civilian, and possessing weaponry in Waraq district, northern Giza in February 2016.
7fd1877fafef5052ad8d02d7b7f62cd2:
An Egyptian court has sentenced 11 people to death by hanging for involvement in a deadly gunfire over car washing.
The sentences were issued by the Cairo Criminal Court on Tuesday against the 11 defendants convicted of murder, show of force and terrorizing the public.
The convicts include six brothers.
The verdict can be appealed.
Two people were killed and five injured in the gunbattle that dates back to April last year in the working-class area of Old Cairo.
The fight started with a fracas after one of the convicts blocked the traffic in a local street by washing cars as a source of a livelihood.
The quarrel developed into a pitched fight between relatives of both sides, who used firearms.
The two dead were pedestrians, who were caught in the crossfire.
In recent months, Egyptian authorities have toughened penalties against using water in car washing and spraying streets in an attempt to conserve water.
Offenders can face a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds (Dh4,246) and a jail term of up to six months.
Egypt is worried that a disputed dam being constructed by Ethiopia on the Nile will cut Egypt’s share of the river’s waters.
Last week, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan—three riparian countries—failed to clinch a deal on the hydroelectric Renaissance Dam building.
5d254d31006102752f8a5a8999efde77:
Egypt’s military criminal court referred 36 members of the ISIS terrorist group to the Grand Mufti after they were sentenced to death for attacks against churches in the country.
The defendants are suspected of involvement in bombings that hit three Coptic churches, killing at least 70 people.
Egypt requires that courts refer cases to the Grand Mufti for consideration of the death penalty ahead of a final verdict.
The court will issue a final verdict on May 15.
Eleven of the 36 are being tried in absentia.
Some of the suspects held leadership positions in ISIS and formed cells to carry out the church attacks.
Some of the defendants are also accused of carrying out an attack on a checkpoint in Egypt’s Western Desert that killed at least eight policemen in 2017.
07e413514b29fa7539c2b0cf4f449880:
Egypt's former anti-corruption chief Hisham Geneina will face military trial for saying a presidential candidate he supported had documents damning to state officials.
Geneina had been a top campaign aide to Sami Anan, whom the military also detained after he announced he would stand in last month's presidential election against incumbent Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.
Geneina had said the documents Anan allegedly possessed "revolve around political events and crises Egyptian society has passed through" since the January 2011 uprising.
Moataz Wadnan, the journalist who conducted the interview, has also been arrested.
a4b2c2f275a2eb3e4fa9dc06ef6e4c57:
Egypt’s Court of Cassation will hand down its unchallenged ruling on the retrial of former Muslim Brotherhood Supreme Guide Mohamed Badie over charges of inciting violence in the “Rabaa operation room case” on Saturday.
Badie, along with 17 other defendants, have appealed against court verdicts ranging from life imprisonment to five years in jail.
Badie was the eighth leader of the banned Muslim Brotherhood (MB) organization.
Badie was arrested on August 19, 2013 as part of a nation-wide crackdown on Brotherhood leaders in the wake of increasing violence and protests after two Brotherhood sit-ins were forcefully dispersed on August 14, 2013.
Badie is still being tried in 11 known cases, mainly over charges of “inciting violence.”
Badie and former Islamist President Mohamed Morsi, with 20 co-defendants, are being retried over charges of “spying” for Palestine’s Gaza-based Hamas movement.
Badie is being charged with “staging an armed gathering in Rabaa Square, illegally possessing and handling weapons, blocking driveways, and deliberately vandalizing public property, along with other counts relating to murdering policemen and citizens” in the Rabaa sit-in dispersal case.
Badie and 27 co-defendants are being tried in the case of breaking into Egyptian prisons, known as the break-in of the eastern border in 2011.
Badie and 12 other defendants are being retried by the Cairo Criminal Court over charges of inciting murder against peaceful demonstrators outside the MB Guidance Bureau in Moqattam, Cairo in 2013.
Badie and 13 other Brotherhood members are being retried in the “al-Bahr al-Azam case”, in which they are charged with “inciting clashes” in al-Bahr al-Azam district, Giza, causing death of five people.
Badie and 13 co-defendants were charged with killing 10 and attempting to murder 20 others in the clashes outside Istiqama Mosque in Giza.
Badie is being charged over inciting violence in the clashes in El Idwa, Minya governorate, following the Rabaa sit-in dispersal on August 14, 2013.
A total of 105 defendants, including Badie, are being tried in the “Ismailia incidents case”, in which they are charged with inciting violence, and killing and injuring people in clashes between pro-Muslim Brotherhood supporters and security forces outside the Brotherhood office in Ismailia in July 2014.
Badie and Brotherhood members Mohamed El-Beltagy and Safwat Hegazy were sentenced to 10 years in prison by a military court in December 2015 over charges of inciting riots in Suez.
Badie and 92 other defendants are being retried over charges of “setting fire” to state institutions in Beni Suef following the dispersal of the Rabaa sit-in.
4e58bbe732460a1f5d37abd971a65274:
An Egyptian court upheld the life sentence against Mohamed Badie, head of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood group, over violence charges.
The Court of Cassation, Egypt's top court that gives final verdicts, upheld the verdicts of life and rigorous imprisonment against Badie and 17 other Brotherhood members for their involvement in the armed sit-in and attempted murder.
The defendants are accused of scheming a terrorist plot that aimed at vandalizing vital government facilities and places of worship.
They are also charged with directing the Brotherhood members to defy the government and to spread chaos in the country.
Most Brotherhood leaders, including ousted former President Mohamed Morsi and Badie, are currently in custody.
Morsi himself is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence on charges of inciting clashes between his supporters and opponents outside a presidential palace in Cairo in late 2012 that left 10 people killed.
17aeb26cfacc0a743eb0a44ed6ea3ef6:
An Egyptian court upheld a life sentence against Mohamed Badie, the leader of the banned Muslim Brotherhood, over 2013 violence.
The court of cassation, Egypt’s top court, rejected an appeal by Badie and others against verdicts issued against them last May in the case known as “the Rabaa Operations Room” trial.
The case relates to a sit-in in Rabaa to support ousted President Mohamed Mursi who hailed from the Muslim Brotherhood.
The sit-in was forcibly dispersed by security forces, leaving hundreds dead.
Badie and two others were sentenced to life imprisonment in the case, 15 others were sentenced to five years while 21 people were acquitted.
The defendants were charged with leading an illegally founded organization, plotting to stir chaos and publishing false news among other crimes.
Authorities outlawed the Brotherhood after Mursi was ousted, and arrested thousands of its supporters.
Decisions made by the court of cassation are final and cannot be appealed.
Saturday’s life sentence is the third against Badie.
61a1f6aa53d64f009f5bbaa4617c861a:
Egypt's former anti-corruption chief Hisham Genena has been referred to a military court for trial on charges of spreading false news harmful to the military establishment.
Genena ran alongside former military chief-of-staff Sami Anan as a member of his short-lived presidential campaign before Anan was detained in January.
Genena was arrested and put under investigation by the military prosecutor in February over comments he had allegedly made in an interview with the HuffPost Arabi news website.
Genena's lawyer, Ali Taha, gave no further details about the charges he faced.
Genena is due in court on April 16.
Family members say Genena is depressed and in poor physical condition.
bfc47e2590ad759337b5c52c36c6cbc9:
An Egyptian court upheld a life sentence against Mohamed Badie, the leader of the banned Muslim Brotherhood, over 2013 violence.
The court of cassation, Egypt's top court, rejected an appeal by Badie and others against verdicts issued against them last May in the case known as "the Rabaa Operations Room" trial.
The case relates to a sit-in in Rabaa to support ousted President Mohamed Morsi who hailed from the Muslim Brotherhood.
The sit-in, which began after the army ousted Morsi, was forcibly dispersed by security forces, leaving hundreds dead.
Badie and two others were sentenced to life imprisonment in the case, 15 others were sentenced to five years while 21 people were acquitted.
The defendants were charged with leading an illegally founded organisation, plotting to stir chaos and publishing false news among other crimes.
Authorities outlawed the Brotherhood after Morsi was ousted and arrested thousands of its supporters.
They also dissolved its Freedom and Justice Party, which Morsi led.
Decisions made by the court of cassation are final and cannot be appealed.
Saturday's life sentence is the third against Badie.
dac8938b9d85dda727b809c90a5c61fc:
Egypt's Court of Cassation upheld death sentences against four defendants convicted of terror-related charges in the 2015 "Ousim terrorist cell case.”
The court also upheld jail sentences ranging between 15 years to life for 29 defendants in the same case.
The defendants were convicted of forming and operating a terrorist cell with the aim of undermining the constitution, targeting public and private property, threatening law enforcement officers, as well as a failed assassination attempt on a judge in March 2015.
The defendants were also accused of orchestrating and carrying out a number of terrorist attacks in Giza governorate.
The Sunday Court of Cassation verdict is not subject to appeal.
2b535bcb6f9494e1f3598c1c62c9b6a7:
Egyptian top court removed 31 members and supporters of the Muslim Brotherhood group from the terrorist list over a case related to the deadly protests in 2014.
The 2014 protests erupted after then army chief Abdel-Fattah al-Sisi announced running for president a year after he ousted former Islamist President Mohamed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood.
Cairo Criminal Court sentenced 17 defendants to 25 years in jail, nine to 15 years, four to 10 years and two to seven years while acquitting 15 of the charges of committing acts of violence.
Egypt has been facing a wave of terror attacks that have killed hundreds of policemen and soldiers, as well as civilians since Morsi's ouster in early July 2013.
A Sinai-based militant group affiliated with the regional terror group Islamic State has claimed responsibility for most of the attacks.
The Egyptian forces have killed hundreds of terrorists and arrested thousands of suspects during the country's anti-terror war declared by Sisi following Morsi's ouster.
3cf21cf239edf26699020cf0c9de6cf9:
An Egyptian court sentenced four Colombian nationals to 10 years in prison each for their involvement in five burglaries in New Cairo.
The court acquitted the defendants for six other thefts.
The defendants formed a gang specialised in burglarising homes in the wealthy 5th Settlement district in new Cairo.
The defendants confessed to breaking into five villas.
Christian Camillo, Jorman Fenanand, Michael Humberto and Christian Esteban were arrested by a special police unit at an apartment in downtown Cairo's Abdeen district on 8 April.
Police found gold and diamond jewelry weighing about 2kg, as well as cash in several currencies upon searching the apartment.
8125fcf1f4ac80abfa4598a0bb064cef:
Cairo’s Court of Cassation upheld a primary ruling to list 46 defendants as terrorists over the killing of former Attorney General Hisham Barakat.
Egypt’s top court of appeals rejected a challenge filed by the 46 defendants to cancel their terror designation.
Cairo Criminal Court sentenced 28 defendants to death, 15 defendants to life imprisonment, eight defendants to 15 years in prison and 15 defendants to 10 years in prison for being involved in the assassination of Barakat.
The defendants are facing other charges that include being associated with Palestinian militant group Hamas, aiming to foment instability in the country and illegally possessing firearms.
Barakat was assassinated on June 29, 2015, when a car bomb detonated in his car outside his home in Cairo’s Heliopolis neighborhood.
148ac755c3afdb70c47d0401c7fec0e6:
A military court will pronounce the verdict on Hisham Geneina, former head of the Central Auditing Organization, on April 24, over his controversial statements to HuffPost Arabi.
Geneina was arrested on February 13 following his statement about Sami Anan, the now arrested former presidential candidate, where Geneina said that Anan possesses documents against the country's current leadership, which he kept outside Egypt.
Geneina's lawyers, including Farid al Deeb, expressed objection to their client’s trial by a military court, claiming that Geneina’s case does not fall under the jurisdiction of the military court.
Military spokesperson Tamer el-Refai said that the Egyptian army will investigate the statements, saying that they drive a wedge between the Egyptian army and the citizens amid a war against terrorism.
Anan Junior accused Geneina of slander and spreading false information on the behalf of his father.
422880eb5e1dbfac1fb4816d873d92bc:
An Egyptian military court sentenced former anti-corruption chief Hisham Geneina to five years in jail for making statements against the army.
Geneina claimed that a presidential candidate had secret documents allegedly damaging to the army.
Geneina was detained in February for "spreading news that harms the armed forces" following an interview he gave to Huffpost Arabi.
The journalist who conducted the interview, Moataz Wadnan, was also arrested.
Geneina was sacked by President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi as head of the Central Auditing Authority in 2016 after he was accused of exaggerating the cost of corruption in Egypt.
bd27802918e0cde22a2962e430b364b9:
An Algerian court has sentenced a Liberian national to death for "spying for Israel."
Six other individuals of different sub-Saharan nationalities were sentenced to 10 years in prison with fines of up to 20 million Algerian dinars (26,000 U.S. dollars).
The defendants were charged with spying, conspiracy to seriously undermine Algeria's security, and glorifying terrorism.
The defendants pleaded not guilty, claiming that they entered Algeria in order to reach Europe.
The seven people were arrested in January 2016 by security services in downtown Ghardaia amid a violent sectarian strife in the region.
31a1746faadd760cd2b5f0f03a0623f5:
Egypt’s Court of Cassation overruled a verdict to add 161 defendants on terror lists on charges of establishing a terrorist group affiliated with ISIS.
The Court of Cassation ordered that the decision be reviewed before the Criminal Court.
Seventy-eight defendants had filed appeals against the Cairo Criminal Court's decision to blacklist them.
The Public Prosecution had charged the accused with joining an illegal group, aimed at obstructing the constitution and laws and preventing state institutions from carrying out their duties.
The Court of Cassation set a hearing for July 10 to issue a verdict on the appeals submitted by 119 Muslim Brotherhood leaders and members against their blacklisting.
The defendants on terror lists include a number of Muslim Brotherhood Guidance Office members, most notably Mahmoud Ezzat, Mohammed Abdulrahman al-Morsi and Mahmoud Hussein.
6f7ed4126b1fe9452496a515b482e1bd:
Egypt's first democratically elected president Mohamed Morsi was in court on charges of "communication with Hamas".
The prosecution charged Morsi and a number of others with crimes including communicating with foreign organisations outside the country in order to commit terrorist acts in the country, disclosing defence secrets to a foreign state and those working for its interests, financing terrorism, military training to achieve the purposes of the Muslim Brotherhood, and committing acts that undermine the country's independence, unity and territorial integrity.
Morsi has been on trial in a number of cases since his ouster in a military coup in 2013.
Human rights groups have repeatedly lambasted the Egyptian government for its treatment of the former president and other political prisoners who they say are being held on trumped up charges.
7f4066439b8ffc2780510cf184ce8033:
Egypt's top court upheld the death penalty for six Muslim Brotherhood loyalists for attacking a police station in 2013.
The court reduced the execution verdicts against three defendants to 25-year imprisonment, upheld the 25-year jail for 59 defendants and acquitted 47 others.
The convicts stormed a police station in Minya's Matay town, stole weapons, killed a senior policeman, attempted to murder others, allowed detainees to escape and set fire to the police station.
The convicts were supporters of ousted Islamist President Mohamed Morsi and committed the acts of violence following the security dispersal of pro-Morsi sit-ins in 2013.
Morsi was removed by the army in 2013 in response to mass protests against his rule and his Muslim Brotherhood group.
Morsi is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence for inciting deadly clashes and a 25-year jail term for leaking classified documents.
Egypt has been facing a wave of terror attacks since Morsi's ouster, with a Sinai-based militant group affiliated with the Islamic State claiming responsibility for most of the attacks.
The Egyptian forces have killed hundreds of terrorists and arrested thousands of suspects during the country's anti-terror war.
6d097899d9f2a90d5cf905c67f0b9e4f:
A Cairo criminal court sentenced 13 policemen to between three and five years in prison for breaking an assembly law when they gathered to demand higher wages and better working conditions in 2015 and 2016.
The policemen were also convicted of detaining another police officer they claimed had mistreated a colleague in their home province of Sharqiya, in the Nile Delta.
The Cairo court of Cassation confirmed death sentences passed on six people, and life sentences on 59 others, accused of storming and setting fire to a police station in the southern province of Minya in 2013.
93672f22d4ff26f2d0fc417a0bfd2bb1:
Egypt’s prosecutor-general Nabil Sadek summoned five Cairo officials for questioning after heavy rainfall last week caused floods that damaged property in New Cairo.
The officials summoned are the deputy head of the New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA), the municipal head of New Cairo, chairman of the Great Cairo Sewage Company, and the chief legal officers at NUCA and the Holding Company for Water and Wastewater.
Residents of New Cairo took to social media to express their frustration at the perceived negligence by officials and emergency departments.
The public prosecutor also ordered the formation of a committee of urban development and engineering professors as well as members of the country’s main anti-corruption body to inspect drainage systems at the affected area.
The committee is tasked with identifying the reason behind the floodwater accumulation and the power outage, as well as estimate the amount of money spent on maintenance and take legal action if any wrongdoing is determined to have taken place.
de2e082e50e6b6ae60875ac6f86b5641:
Egypt's general prosecution referred 318 members of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Sinai Province (ISIL-SP) to the military court on charges of planning terrorist attacks against military and police forces.
The list of defendants included the Egyptian national fugitive Tarek el Zomor, former chairman of Building and Development Party.
Tarek el Zomor is accused of funding the terrorist activities in Egypt following July 2013.
Tarek el Zomor was among terrorists who assassinated former Egyptian President Anwar Sadat during a military parade on October 6, 1981.
Tarek el Zomor is currently the Chairman of Al Jama’a Al-Islamiyya and the Building and Development Party.
f207df240d6af6fd60afe414b8e0c5fb:
Egypt's judicial authorities sentenced 11 members of the Muslim Brotherhood group, which Cairo considers a terrorist organization.
An Egyptian court accused 170 ISIS elements of photographing an air base and targeting vital installations in the case known as "filming the Belbeis airbase."
The court set the hearing on June 12 to issue the verdicts for 170 ISIS elements.
The indictment added that the terrorist elements have also received by illegal means one of the country’s defense secrets by taking photos, using a mobile phone, for Belbeis air base in preparation for targeting it.
Egypt’s security forces launched an all-out offensive against militants in February, deploying tens of thousands of troops and police backed by fighter-jets, helicopter gunships, navy vessels and tanks in Sinai and in the Western Desert.
Egypt has been battling ISIS elements for years, but the insurgency gathered steam and grew deadlier after the 2013 ouster by the military, then led by Sisi, of Mohammed Morsi.
bd79efa4a88e0cf702e847e575f3cbde:
An Egyptian criminal court has placed 169 members of the banned Muslim Brotherhood group on the country's terror list.
The defendants are facing charges of conspiring to infiltrate state institutions with the aim of overthrowing the regime by force and spreading chaos in the country.
The court’s decision is based on state security investigations, which revealed that the defendants attempted to revive the group's activities by recruiting new members to its armed wings, spread rumors and provided financial and logistical assistance to the Brotherhood.
Under the country’s anti-terrorism law, any person placed on the terror list is subject to a travel ban and having their assets frozen.
Egypt's terror list contains over 1,500 names, including top Brotherhood leaders.
97e8906e2b4c6afbb26f589f93305f6f:
Egyptian police detained Amal Fathy, a member of the banned April 6 youth movement, for posting a video criticizing the government's handling of sexual harassment and worsening living conditions.
Amnesty International condemned the arrest as a "new low in Egypt's crackdown on freedom of expression."
Fathy's husband, Mohamed Lotfy, a human rights lawyer, was detained with her but released three hours later.
Fathy is being held for 15 days for questioning on charges of incitement to overthrow the ruling system, publishing lies, and misusing social media.
Egyptian media criticized Fathy for using foul language in the video.
A security source said Fathy is accused of insulting the Egyptian state by posting a video containing swearing and defamation.
c92518d4cb92cf75032a246b935154d6:
A Cairo court in Egypt ordered 20 Muslim Brotherhood members to be placed on terrorist lists for the next five years.
The court based its decision on proof that the accused were terrorists because some of them were leaders of the Brotherhood.
The 20 terror suspects are charged with purchasing weapons and arms, and receiving funds through Brotherhood leaderships abroad.
The Cairo Criminal Court set August 4 as the date for the retrial of seven defendants in the so-called Tanta terror cell case.
The suspects are charged with forming a terror cell in the western city of Tanta for the purpose of attacking the army and police.
ae871afd6c35753322f195cc1eb1f4cc:
An Egyptian court acquitted two police officers of torturing to death a lawyer while in detention three years ago.
The ruling can be appealed.
The lawyer, Kareem Hamdi, was arrested on suspicion of belonging to the banned Muslim Brotherhood and involvement in its violence.
Hamdi died inside a police station in the northern Cairo district of Matariya.
Lawyers accused police of torturing Hamdi to death allegedly to extract confessions from him.
The country’s chief prosecutor ordered both officers from the National Security Agency to stand trial on charges of torturing the lawyer to death.
In December 2015, a court sentenced the two to five years in prison each.
In October 2016, the Court of Cassation, Egypt’s top appeals tribunal, revoked the verdict and ordered a retrial for both defendants.
Egyptian authorities have pursued a relentless crackdown on Islamists since 2013 when the military toppled president Mohammad Mursi of the Brotherhood following massive protests against his rule.
Rights groups have repeatedly accused the government of ignoring police’s purported violations.
Authorities have downplayed the alleged abuses as isolated acts, vowing to bring any wrongdoer to justice.
In recent years, several policemen have been handed down varying jail terms in separate torture cases in Egypt.
Police abuses were seen as a major catalyst for the 2011 revolt that forced long-time president Hosni Mubarak out of power.
73938bc24f092056c2482ada90539467:
An Egyptian court has acquitted two police officers of charges of torturing and murdering a prominent lawyer in 2015.
Egypt's prosecutor has referred some 278 terror suspects to a military court on charges of joining two breakaway Muslim Brotherhood factions.
The news of the overturned conviction comes amid controversy over a leaked video released last week that appears to show a child being executed at close range in Egypt's Sinai Peninsula by an army officer, dating back to 2015.
In February Amnesty International condemned the escalating "human rights crisis" in Egypt in its annual World Report, citing the country's endemic arbitrary arrests and detentions of hundreds, as well as the new legal restrictions imposed on NGOs and authorities turning a blind eye to torture.
In September, the Egyptian government pledged to take action against Human Rights Watch after it released a damning report on state torture.
President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi told US officials in New York that human rights should not be judged from a Western perspective, arguing that Egypt had taken numerous measures to ensure the economic and social wellbeing of its citizens.
1a15724a5e5459a57464cf187d00d3bf:
An Ismailia criminal court issued preliminary death sentences to 13 defendants convicted of escaping El-Mostakbal prison in 2016.
The court has referred the case to the country's grand mufti for a non-binding opinion on the death sentences.
The defendants include members of Ansar Beit Al-Maqdis terrorist organisation, now known as Daesh Sinai.
A final sentence will be issued by the court on 12 July.
390d57fa0b462181b72fe1c4a6d26679:
Egypt's Prosecutor-General Nabil Sadek referred 278 defendants belonging to the Muslim Brotherhood group to military court for leading and joining the banned armed groups Hasm and Lewaa El-Thawra.
The defendants carried out 12 terrorist operations in several governorates, targeting police officers, manufacturing car bombs, and attacking vital installations and public figures.
The defendants supplied the two groups with money, explosives, weaponry, ammunition, and other logistical support.
Fugitive Brotherhood leaders in Turkey plotted with fugitive members in Egypt to rebuild the group's armed wing and carry out hostile acts against Egyptian officials and institutions.
Fifty-two defendants confessed to their crimes, and some received military training in Sudan on explosives manufacturing.
The defendants possessed 100 machine guns, 11,000 rounds of ammunition, 70 explosive devices, 13 landmines, seven cars, and military uniforms.
The Brotherhood assembled members in 17 governorates under the name Hasm and Lewaa El-Thawra to plot terrorist attacks.
Brotherhood leaders provided financial and logistical support, including 25 locations for manufacturing and storing explosives.
Three locations in Beheira and Alexandria stored weaponry, RDX explosives, and vehicles for terrorist attacks.
The groups carried out assassinations and attempted assassinations against policemen, governors, and public figures in Daqahliya, Fayoum, and Damietta.
Hasm claimed responsibility for attacks against Egyptian security personnel since 2016, including the assassination of a senior policeman in Fayoum and an assassination attempt against former Grand Mufti Ali Gomaa.
Lewaa Al-Thawra claimed responsibility for the assassination of a high-ranking army officer in Qalyoubia governorate in October 2017.
5ee7b6b7925cd080e92e37f817485bde:
Egypt's prosecutor general, Nabil Sadeq, referred 278 suspected Muslim Brotherhood members to military trial on "terrorism" charges.
141 of the 278 people referred for trial are already in detention.
The suspects are facing charges including joining Brotherhood-linked militant groups Lewaa al-Thawra and Hasam.
The suspects are also accused of carrying out 12 "terrorist operations" including targeting and killing police officers and personnel.
Sunday's announcement comes after 555 people were referred to military trial last week, accused of belonging to a branch of ISIS in the Sinai Peninsula.
06ee7f8a1bb3399a8a90371122f5309e:
Egyptian military court sentenced Ismail Alexandrani, a prominent journalist and expert on extremist movements in the Sinai peninsula, to 10 years in prison.
Alexandrani was arrested in November 2015 and accused of publishing military secrets and belonging to the banned Muslim Brotherhood.
Alexandrani was also accused of spreading information that could harm national security outside the country in interviews with the media and in articles.
Alexandrani's lawyer said they will appeal the verdict.
Alexandrani had been in pretrial detention for two and a half years since his arrest in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada after he returned from a work trip in Berlin.
Alexandrani was an expert on extremist movements in North Sinai, where security forces are fighting an insurgency led by ISIS.
Alexandrani had been to Germany to deliver lectures on the political situation in Egypt.
Alexandrani was also known for his anti-regime writings and for criticising the military's role in politics.
Alexandrani was a contributor to publications including the French online magazine Orient XXI.
Co-defendant Walid Mohareb was also sentenced to 10 years in prison in the same trial.
The verdict "exemplifies the government's vicious retaliation against journalists who report on sensitive issues", Human Rights Watch Middle East director Sarah Leah Whitson said.
35d382178f14fee2fb14ee9837c4b885:
Islamic scholar Tariq Ramadan has lost an appeal for early release ahead of his trial in France over rape allegations by four women.
Ramadan, who is being treated behind bars for multiple sclerosis, was not in court to hear Tuesday’s ruling.
Ramadan's lawyer argued that testimony from his accusers contained "contradictions" and that Ramadan should be held at home and surrender his passport.
Prosecutors argued Ramadan should stay in detention over fears that he could potentially flee France and also to protect the women who made the allegations against him.
Ramadan’s first accuser, Henda Ayari, 41, is a feminist activist who previously practised a conservative strain of Islam. She says Ramadan raped her in a Paris hotel room in 2012.
A second woman, who is disabled, claims that Ramadan raped and beat her in a hotel in the southeastern city of Lyon in 2009.
The third accuser, a French Muslim woman who is using the pseudonym "Marie", came forward in early March and claims to have suffered multiple rapes in France, Brussels and London between 2013 and 2014.
A fourth woman has filed rape charges in Geneva against Ramadan.
Ramadan has denied wrongdoing and is suing one of his accusers, Ayari, for slander.
22a7c9d8b409db75dfbf13b4f4e3f95e:
Amnesty International has asked the Algerian authorities to release a blogger, Merzoug Touati, who faces the death penalty on “espionage charges.”
Touati interviewed an Israeli foreign ministry spokesperson in which he disputes accusations by the Algerian authorities that the Israeli authorities were involved in protests in Algeria.
Touati faces charges relating to a Facebook post and YouTube video that authorities claim encouraged civil unrest.
Touati has been in detention since January 2017.

The annual al-Quds Day march in Berlin features frequent calls about killing Israelis, Zionist conspiracies and chants of “free Palestine from the river to the sea.”
Flags of terrorist groups like Hamas and Hezbollah are on display at the al-Quds Day march in Berlin, and imams regularly preach anti-Semitic verses from the Quran to the crowd.
Some incidents documented at the Quds Day march in Berlin have been classified by authorities as forms of far-right anti-Semitism, independent watchdog groups have discovered.
Critics say the march example and other mislabeled incidents are facilitating attempts to politicize anti-Semitism and complicating the apparently losing battle to solve it.
Germany’s Interior Ministry did not respond to JTA’s request for comment.
Doubts about the German Interior Ministry’s methodology have become more pronounced as its data have increasingly diverged with information from across Western Europe — and from the perceptions of German Jews themselves.
In France, more than half of anti-Semitism incidents, and virtually all the violent ones, are perpetrated by immigrants from Muslim countries or their descendants, according to the National Bureau of Vigilance Against Anti-Semitism.
In Britain, the Community Security Trust suggests that far-right perpetrators are responsible for 50-60 percent of the incidents where victims offered a physical description of their attackers.
In the Netherlands, the previous director of CIDI, the country’s foremost watchdog on anti-Semitism, said that Muslims and Arabs are responsible for about 70 percent of all cases recorded in any given year.
In a 2016 survey of hundreds of German Jews who had experienced anti-Semitic incidents, 41 percent said the perpetrator was “someone with a Muslim extremist view” and another 16 percent said it was someone from the far left.
Only 20 percent of German Jews who had experienced anti-Semitic incidents identified their aggressors as belonging to the far-right.
A German court ruled that anti-Semitism was not behind the attempt by three Palestinians to set fire to a synagogue in the city of Wuppertal in 2014.
Some critics believe that there is a political dimension to the apparent reluctance of German authorities to blame anti-Semitism on Muslim immigrants.
The government of German Chancellor Angela Merkel has faced considerable criticism, including that she is importing anti-Semitism, over her decision to let in more than 2 million immigrants from Syria and the Middle East since 2015.
A study by the Berlin-based EVZ foundation claims that there is no connection between anti-Semitism and immigration, despite claims by some Jews to the contrary.
Rabbi Andrew Baker, director of international affairs for the American Jewish Committee and the point man on anti-Semitism of the OSCE intergovernmental organization, criticized the EVZ foundation study, saying that the report’s authors “ignore the data, dismiss the problem, and blame the victims.”
The top intelligence agency in Germany recently published a 40-page analysis of rising anti-Semitism by Islamist extremists that was welcomed by Jewish leaders.
The German government’s system for classifying anti-Semitic incidents is flawed, said Laszlo Bernat Veszpremy, who has researched anti-Semitism among recent immigrants to Europe.
In France and Belgium, authorities are frequently accused of downplaying or sugarcoating left-wing and immigrant anti-Semitism.
A former police commissioner and founder of France’s National Bureau for Vigilance Against Anti-Semitism, or BNVCA, said that he no longer has full confidence that anti-Semitic hate crimes in France are handled properly.
The French National Consultative Commission on Human Rights, a government watchdog, wrote in its annual report for 2016 that a “significant part of the anti-Semitic acts (actions and threats) pertains to neo-Nazi ideology, whereas in most other cases the perpetrators’ motivations are difficult to ascertain.”
The lawyer for the country’s federal watchdog against racism, UNIA, in 2017 protested the hate speech conviction of a Palestinian man who shouted about killing Jews at an anti-Israel demonstration.
Belgian prosecutors recently dismissed a criminal complaint filed against a Turkish cafe owner who in 2014 placed a sign on his business saying dogs are welcome at his business near Liege, “but Jews are not.”

Nagorno-Karabakh, with an area of 4,400 square kilometers and a population of 150,000, was attached to Azerbaijan in 1924 by Josef Stalin, despite its predominantly Armenian population.
Stalin's gerrymandering also included dividing the Kurdish majority enclave of Lachin between Armenia and Azerbaijan and attaching Talesh, a non-Azeri coastal land, to Azerbaijan.
In 1991, the Armenian population of Nagorno-Karabakh expelled the Azeri minority and established their own autonomous republic, with support from Armenia and Russia.
Azerbaijan, with support from Israel, has superiority in armament in the current round of fighting.
Turkey has cast itself as Azerbaijan's principal backer, while depicting Russia and Iran as Armenia's allies.
Iran is facing pressure from within to support Azerbaijan, but is also concerned about the introduction of Syrian militants into the Azeri forces and the potential for spillover into Iranian territory.
The conflict could provoke uncontrollable reactions in Iran, where an estimated 20 million Azeri-speakers live.
If Azerbaijan wins, Turkey, Israel, and the United States would be seen as the victors, while Iran would be seen as indifferent to Azerbaijan's aspirations.
If Armenia wins, Russia and Israel would likely be seen as co-winners, again leaving Iran isolated.
The war is likely to produce only losers, with Azerbaijan unlikely to regain full control of Nagorno-Karabakh, Armenia facing territorial losses and a refugee crisis, Turkey potentially being dragged into a fifth war, Israel forced to choose sides, Russia losing its claim as peacemaker, and Iran facing geopolitical and ideological setbacks.

UN chief Antonio Guterres on Sunday called on both sides to respect the new ceasefire and condemned the attacks on civilians, in particular Saturday's deadly missile strike on Ganja.

Egyptian companies are expected to build restaurants, hotels, resorts, 35 hospitals in ten governorates and develop natural gas-fired power plants.
4ed25ea3194b06c86f490651ea5f133a:
President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi inspected developmental road projects in Old Cairo and East Cairo.
A network of bridges has been constructed to link Old Cairo's Civilizations Axis area with the main roads of Cairo.
The historic Ain Al-Sira area and the vicinity of the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization in Old Cairo are being developed.
Slums in the vicinity of Old Cairo's Al-Sayeda Aisha district have been removed, and residents have been moved to new cities.
The state plans to restore Old Cairo's civilizational splendor and historic heritage, including the Fustat area, the Cairo Citadel Aqueduct, the Religions Complex, and historic mosques.
President Sisi inspected road projects in the districts of Nasr City, Heliopolis, and Autostrad in East Cairo.
President Sisi urged officials and supervisors to adhere to the timeframes set to implement these projects in accordance to the highest standards.
367840b79a3fa17ffd582ba6177b0905:
Two Czech social influencers visited Hurghada in a trip organized by the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities to promote tourism.
The Czech bloggers went diving in the Red Sea and visited the Hurghada Museum, where they praised the display of Tutankhamun's artefacts.
The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM), which was listed as one of the top attractions to visit this year by CNN, is scheduled for inauguration this year.
The Czech bloggers also visited the Giza Pyramids, Saqqara Necropolis, the Step Pyramid of Djoser, and Khan Al-Khalili Bazaar in Cairo.
The Czech bloggers will next head to Luxor to tour its archaeological attractions.
Egypt has received 1.4 million tourists since reopening its seaside resorts to international flights in July.
cfa99e69e7c13d7026219331f2770c50:
Egypt and France will finalize details of bilateral projects under Egypt’s sustainable development 2030 agenda during the visit of French Minister of Finance in February.
Egypt and France have begun negotiating the allocation and execution of development financing projects via French companies.
The bilateral partnership between Egypt and France aims to achieve the UN’s sustainable development goals and support Egypt’s national agenda 2030.
In December, Egypt and France signed three financing agreements worth €715.6 million to support the health, transportation, education, and water sectors.
The history of cooperation between Egypt and France dates back to 1974, with an economic cooperation portfolio worth €7.5 billion.
The current cooperation portfolio between Egypt and France rounds up to €1 billion.
3fcefc1e1efb3f3237ad6ff444c36bf7:
Egypt's government has launched the second phase of initiative supporting export companies, with registration opening from 7 February to the end of the month.
The initiative aims to disburse the export companies' arrears from the Export Development Fund (EDF) before the end of the current FY2020/2021 (ending in June).
The second phase of the initiative will be executed with the same conditions of the first phase.
The initiative contributes in providing cash liquidity that enables export companies to meet their financial obligations, keep their labour force and boost the competitiveness of Egyptian products in international markets.
In September, Egypt’s government launched the first phase of the initiative that targeted instant and cash repayment of the entirety of export companies’ arrears from the EDF before the end of 2020 at a repay acceleration discount of 15 percent.
1069 export companies benefitted from the first phase, with total disbursements of EGP 13.5 billion.
The initiative is implemented in collaboration with the banking system, as the finance ministry deposits a guarantee at the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) to allow for the payment of the arrears for the companies that are willing to pay their entire dues.
The finance ministry will repay these sums and their proceeds to the banks that contributed to the initiative over three years.
The government disbursed EGP 21 billion over a year in order to support the exports sector through six initiatives.
2500 export companies benefitted from the other five initiatives with a total of EGP 5.6 billion disbursed for the exports during FY2019/2020 as well as EGP 2.4 billion disbursed from July to November 2020.
The cabinet has approved five initiatives since October 2019 that aimed to settle the exporters’ arrears through June 2019.
7c85545e062b749d3bc3e1e77ed2a34e:
Egypt’s Minister of International Cooperation, Rania Al-Mashat, met with the Ambassador of Belgium, François Cornet D’Elzius, to discuss future plans of bilateral cooperation between the countries.
Egypt and Belgium have been working on various agreements with the European Union regarding projects listed for development financing for 2022.
Belgium is eager to further cooperate with Egypt on the development of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises, and on the establishment of a strong public-private dialogue in the Egyptian business sphere.
Egypt and Belgium have cooperated on the restoration project of the Baron Palace, under the debt-swap programme between both countries, for an agreement worth €2.14 million (EGP 16 million).
The Ministry of International Cooperation secured development financing agreements worth $9.8 billion during 2020; $6.7 billion of which were for financing sovereign projects, and $3.1 billion for supporting the private sector.
ca3887364e47457dc56c3141f6bf3703:
Egypt’s President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi stressed the importance of inter-Arab cooperation in the area of intelligence during the inauguration of the Arab Intelligence Forum 2021 in Cairo.
El-Sisi asserted the importance of empowering the forum as a strong and supportive mechanism for cooperation in intelligence between Arab countries.
The forum should work on a counterterrorism system that depends on exchanging expertise.
El-Sisi stressed the importance of Arab countries cooperating to restore stability in all the region’s countries, where terrorist organisations attempt to expand with the support of foreign forces that aim to create chaos to control the resources and capabilities of the Arab world.
The heads of intelligence agencies who participated in the forum stressed the importance of the platform in boosting cooperation to protect Arab national security by exchanging points of view on dealing with the rapid challenges facing the region, especially in counterterrorism, organised crime and radical thought.
6664e76a712654626c5418bd9736230c:
Egypt is adopting a vast infrastructure plan to link nine African countries, including Sudan, with the largest land road in Africa.
The project aims to create a route from Salloum to Benghazi, supporting Egyptian industry and labor and contributing to the transport of goods to Libya.
The development of the railway system comes in parallel with the establishment of the express electric train, aiming to achieve safety and avoid human errors.
The Egyptian state is making great efforts to develop land and dry ports, with a comprehensive plan to establish 13 ports and a logistical center.
The new Egyptian ports aim to facilitate internal and external trade movement, support the Egyptian economy, prevent the accumulation of goods and containers in sea ports and achieve integration between means of transportation.
A total of 35 projects were planned, with a total cost of 15 billion Egyptian pounds ($951,000).
Nine projects have already been completed at a total cost of 300 million pounds, including the construction of the Qustul land port, the Arqin land port, and development of the Taba land port.
5886eb4cfaded506886a820fcead22a2:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry and his Brazilian counterpart, Ernesto Araujo, discussed ways to encourage more cooperation between the private sectors in both countries.
Shoukry and Araujo urged cooperation between private sector companies in agriculture, medical and pharmaceutical research, as well as science and technology.
They also agreed on enhancing commercial relations and investments between Egypt and the Mercosur, the South American trade bloc.
The two ministers affirmed the need for cooperation between the two countries within the framework of the projects that Egypt is implementing in Africa.
They also discussed the latest in the dispute over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
Shoukry stressed to his Brazilian counterpart Egypt's insistence on the need to reach a legally binding agreement on the filling and operating of the Ethiopian dam through engaging in serious talks “without procrastination.”
In 2018, trade exchange between Egypt and Brazil stood at $3.34 billion.
600 made-in-Egypt products exported to Mercosur countries are fully exempt from taxes, as part of the free trade agreement signed between Egypt and the South America trade bloc.
eff8988a7e5b8ee77bf09cd315a018e3:
Egypt and Sudan have conducted quality military exercises, codenamed Eagles of the Nile, for the first time in their history to ensure that both armies remain well-prepared in the face of any regional dangers threatening their countries existence or jeopardising their national security.
Egypt has also reiterated its full support for Sudan’s national security in the face of any regional threats to Sudan’s territorial integrity and stability.
The media in both Egypt and Sudan are tasked with a major role, as both need to engage in a different discourse and make a clean sweep of any misperceptions that may regrettably have been instilled in the minds of average Sudanese and Egyptian people over the decades.
Egypt was never, even in the darkest moments of its relations with Sudan, the kind of bad neighbour that Al-Bashir’s media pretended.
Egypt’s goal to establish an industrial park in Sudan must, therefore, be given top priority, and all the Egyptian bodies concerned should not spare any efforts to realise this goal in the near future.
Thanks to connections between the two countries in terms of land and maritime transportation, it is now much easier to do business than it was, and there are more opportunities to further economic and trade relations between the two peoples.
The economic hardships facing Sudan today should not derail Egyptian entrepreneurs from starting joint projects in favour of the two peoples.
47321de6ec950dcd1fd733c8b5568099:
Sky Abu Dhabi, a real estate subsidiary of the UAE-based Emirati Diamond Group, will invest 15 billion Egyptian pounds ($950 million) in the Egyptian real estate market over the next two years.
Sky Abu Dhabi’s first project will be a 4 billion Egyptian pound investment in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital development.
The project extends over an area of 24 acres and includes the establishment of an integrated urban community consisting of around 1,000 housing units.
The company plans to spend 300 million Egyptian pounds on construction of the project this year, while aiming for sales of 1.5 billion Egyptian pounds in 2021.
The value of the land on which the project is based is estimated at 650 million Egyptian pounds due to the distinctive location.
80 percent of the project consists of residential units and the remaining 20 percent for commercial use.
Sky Abu Dhabi’s portfolio of projects includes 17 projects in the UAE market.
7a54b51214fc2210a202bc8b9399979c:
Pakistan is considering expansions in its densely populated large cities.
Pakistan is keen on benefiting from Egypt’s expertise in social housing.

Egypt and Pakistan are strengthening trade cooperation and developing bilateral scientific and cultural cooperation.
a20e71b8098a35f2afd73cef4383e8c5:
Egypt has been elected to lead the United Nations (UN) Peacebuilding Commission for the first time, succeeding Canada.
Egypt's election to lead the commission's 15th session is a successful outcome of Egyptian diplomacy over a decade and a half in supporting the structure of the UN for peacebuilding since its establishment in 2005.
Egypt assumes the chairmanship in the wake of the successful conclusion of the third five-year comprehensive review process of the United Nations peacebuilding architecture.
Egypt remains fully committed as an African country to ensure the United Nations peacebuilding architecture remains engaged on the continent.
Egypt aims to further boost the commission's role in building back better, while ensuring sustained financing for peacebuilding as a high priority for the commission's ability and effectiveness.
Egypt is also very keen to continue to promote and expand the commission's partnerships with regional and subregional organisations and international financial institutions, with a view to ensure more efficiency and coherence in support of peacebuilding efforts.
6db576aafd64ba6898aa3abd31489e65:
The first phase of a national project to improve living conditions and create job opportunities for over 5,000 poor villages in Egypt was launched.
The first phase of the National Programme for the Development of Egyptian Villages will last until the end of the year and will target improving the quality of life in villages where 57 per cent of Egypt’s population resides.
The rate of poverty in these villages exceeds 55 per cent, and the rates of illiteracy and the percentage of households where women are the bread-winners are higher than in other villages and urban areas.
The villages included in the first phase are in 21 governorates across Egypt.
The project is designed to complement Egypt’s “Decent Life” programme to improve rural communities by ensuring better living conditions, reducing poverty, upgrading infrastructure and improving public services.
The programme also focuses on supporting small and medium enterprises [SMEs] in these villages, improving healthcare units, upgrading the efficiency of irrigation networks, enhancing agricultural and veterinary services and establishing advanced dairy collection centres.
The plan will include the relocation of public service offices in governorates and villages, and connecting them electronically to the related ministries in their new headquarters in the New Administrative Capital.
Egyptian companies will be tasked with providing the resources needed for the project.
The scheme is expected to provide several job opportunities for youth and revitalise the country’s economy.
7baed6da2684c43a9ad4dce2ba2209f7:
Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi inspected the Integrated Transport Centre project to reduce traffic congestion in Cairo.
The 300 feddan centre includes an international bus station, a transport terminal between governorates, a mall, an administrative complex, recreational areas and restaurants, a hotel and the workshops of Cairo Metro’s fourth line.
The project's location is in the centre of link axes connecting main roads nationwide, with its proximity to Cairo airport allowing for the facilitated mobility of travelers domestically and internationally.
The Suez Road has been upgraded to accommodate nine lanes in each direction, with the development of a road supporting the Ring Road with eight lanes in each direction and the construction of a new road to link the Ring Road, Suez Road and Mohamed Naguib Axis.
El-Sisi ordered an acceleration of implementation rates to reduce the traffic congestion on the main streets, ease the movement of citizens and reduce fuel consumption.
El-Sisi gave directives to ensure close coordination between all state bodies regarding renewing the facilities within the scope of these projects, which includes drainage systems and sanitation networks.
20c6c651af725283a12ba0f135cb7a6a:
GCC Secretary General Nayef Al-Hajraf met President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi and hailed his role in protecting Arab national security.
GCC considers Egypt a main pillar for national security in the Arab region.

GCC supports the Egyptian government in battling terrorism.

Egypt seeks to strengthen cooperation ties with Iraq through supporting development efforts in the country.
Egypt and Iraq reached an oil-for-reconstruction agreement, under which Egyptian companies will implement construction projects in Iraq in return for Iraq providing Egypt with certain quantities of oil.
Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan are targeting cementing cooperation ties in different fields, including oil pipeline power linkages ventures.
Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan met in a tripartite meeting to coordinate positions on issues of mutual concern and the Palestinian cause.
02d2765f2dad963e997705f50936b5e0:
The European Commission and the high representative announced the adoption of a new agenda for the Mediterranean region, including Egypt.
The agenda aims to boost the strategic partnership between the EU and the Mediterranean.
The agenda includes an economic and investment plan that targets boosting the long-term socio-economic recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic in the southern neighbourhood.
Under the new EU's Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI), up to €7 billion for the period 2021 to 2027 will be allocated to its implementation, which can mobilise around €30 billion in private and public investments in the region over the next decade.
The new agenda focuses on five policy areas, including human development, good governance and the rule of law, resilience, prosperity, and digital transition.
The agenda also includes providing support to countries to address security challenges and find solutions to ongoing conflicts, in addition to addressing the challenges of forced displacement and irregular migration, and facilitating safe and legal pathways for migration and mobility.
The agenda concentrates on green transition as well as introducing an economic investment plan for the Southern Neighbours to ensure the quality of life for people in the region improves and economic recovery is realised.
The EU provided support to Egypt mainly through the European Neighbourhood Instrument with €756 million in the period from 2014 to 2020.
f6e137394c378c262b099598f344fb35:
Prime Minister Bisher Al Khasawneh conveyed a verbal message from King Abdullah to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El Sisi, reaffirming the strong brotherly relations between the two countries.
The message highlighted views on issues of mutual interests and in service of Arab issues, foremost of which is the Palestinian cause.
The Egyptian president and the premier emphasized the deep-rooted, historical and strategic Jordanian-Egyptian ties, expressing keenness to further cooperation, notably in the economic and trade fields.
They also emphasized the necessity of bolstering the trilateral cooperation brought forth from the outcomes of the Amman-hosted tripartite summit between King Abdullah, President Sisi and Iraqi Prime Minister Mustafa Al Kadhimi.
Talks also went over expanding the trilateral cooperation to include more Arab nations for the best interests of these countries and their peoples.
Sisi and Khasawneh highlighted the two countries’ “unceasing efforts” towards serving Arab issues, foremost of which is the Palestinian cause, stressing the two countries’ firm stance on the necessity of the establishment of an independent Palestinian state on the June 4, 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital on the basis of the two-state solution, to achieve a fair and comprehensive peace in the region, as well as enhance regional security and stability.
c63302a288a7c8176dae057836fcbbf7:
Egypt's Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and his Jordanian counterpart, Bishr Al-Khasawneh, visited Downtown Cairo to inspect the ongoing development works at Tahrir square.
The development project will extend to sites in and around Tahrir square, including Omar Makram Mosque, the Mogamma government building, the Egyptian Museum, and the newly established Tahrir parking garage.
The project aims to restore the 150-year-old square to its former glory and create a civilised facade symbolising the spirit of ongoing development in the old capital.
The project will involve painting the facades of buildings, planting trees to create green spaces, and decorating the entire square with pure light LEDs to create a festive atmosphere.
The square is already home to a 17-metre obelisk that weighs 90 tons, dating back to the reign of the ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Ramses II, and four ram-headed sphinx statues from Luxor’s Karnak Temple.
The project is funded by the Ministry of Housing, Utilities, and Urban Communities in coordination with Cairo and the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities.
31100741c6d097de56a0d375a7d358ff:
Saudi Arabia wants to promote bilateral strategic cooperation with Egypt on multiple levels.
Saudi Arabia's King Salman bin Abdul-Aziz sent a written message to Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi, emphasizing the deep historical ties between the two countries.
The message stressed the importance of continuing joint work and intensive coordination with Egypt on various regional and international issues.
Saudi Minister of State and Cabinet Member Essam bin Said conveyed the message to El-Sisi in Cairo.
El-Sisi reaffirmed the "special and strategic" relationship between Egypt and Saudi Arabia and its importance for regional stability.
El-Sisi highlighted the "delicate" circumstances and challenges facing Arab countries.
Both sides agreed to continue to reinforce bilateral cooperation and consultation in various fields to achieve the common interests of the Egyptian and Saudi peoples, as well as Arab solidarity bonds.

Egypt's Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry congratulated Mariam Al-Sadiq Al-Mahdi, the new foreign minister in the new Sudanese cabinet, on assuming the post.
Shoukry affirmed to Al-Mahdi Egypt's keenness to enhance bilateral relations with Sudan and to intensify coordination to achieve foster constructive strategic cooperation tying the two countries.
Al-Mahdi expressed to Shoukry deep appreciation to Egypt and expressed her aspiration to continue joint work with the neighboring country to achieve stronger bilateral relations.
Al-Mahdi is the daughter of the late Sadiq Al-Mahdi, the leader of Al-Umma Party and two-time prime minister who passed away late last year.
Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok announced his new cabinet, which consists of 26 ministers, on Monday night.
Al-Mahdi also stressed to the Egyptian foreign minister that enhancing bilateral relations with Egypt during the coming period represents a priority to Sudan.
Shoukry urged in the phone call building on the strong bilateral relations between the two countries to move to further horizons of partnership and cooperation that serve the peoples of the two countries and enhance the historic official and popular ties between the two countries.
Shoukry also wished Sudan and the Sudanese people permanent progress, prosperity and development.
In recent years, Egypt and Sudan have voiced similar concerns in the ongoing dispute with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD).
Both countries have repeatedly affirmed that a reaching a binding legal agreement on the filling and operation of the GERD between all three countries is the only way out of the current stalemate in negotiations.
8a4a147aa69b9c1e126bcb026183745f:
President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi met with Jordanian Prime Minister Bisher Al-Khasawneh to discuss bilateral cooperation in energy, combating terrorism and extremist ideology.
Egypt, Jordan and Iraq are pushing for trilateral cooperation in economy, trade, energy and investment.

They discussed the developments of the peace process in the Middle East in light of the results of the last ministerial meeting of the Arab League.
The officials agreed to work on intensifying international efforts to settle the Palestinian crisis based on international legitimacy resolutions to resume peace negotiations.
Egypt, along with Jordan, France, and Germany, formed the quartet committee in February 2020 to revive the halted Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations.

Jordanian Prime Minister Bisher Khasawneh delivered a verbal message from King Abdullah II to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

Khasawneh and Madbouly noted the joint Jordanian-Egyptian position on consultation and coordination on all issues of common interest to serve Arab issues, foremost of which is the Palestinian cause.

The project will include a main logistical center, research and test centers, areas for entrepreneurship, small businesses and light industries, and a space dedicated to warehouses.
CTP Invest has more than 22 years of experience developing industrial business parks and currently owns projects in more than 100 locations, with a combined area of more than 6.3 million square meters, servicing around 700 clients across various sectors.
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly praised the company and directed the General Authority for Investment to conclude discussions and agree on a model going forward.
9a9439c55f803716e84df321b46b8dc4:

Last year, Ambassador of Egypt to Pakistan Tarek Mohamed Dahroug appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and stability.

Iranians will go to the polls to pick a new president on 18 June.
Brig. Gen (ret.) Hossein Dehghan, the former defence minister-turned advisor to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, is a possible contender.
Dehghan warned about the risks of a tactical conflict with the US escalating into a full-scale war.
Dehghan stressed that Tehran was “not after negotiations for the sake of negotiations”.
Dehghan added that Tehran would not rest until all forces from the US “terror state” were expelled from the Middle East.
Saeed Mohammad, a second brigadier general in the IRGC and former head of the IRGC-controlled Khatam al-Anbiya Construction Headquarter engineering firm, has also announced his intention to run.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the populist conservative who served as president of Iran between 2005 and 2013, has yet to formally express plans to run in the 2021 elections.
Ahmadinejad has consistently ranked number one among prospective voters in a range of informal polling, pulling in up to 47 percent support.
20b2be224322b6748815a0631e234ec7:
Iran opened the door for candidacies for the upcoming presidential vote.
President Hassan Rouhani rejected the decision of the Guardian Council to study the candidates’ applications.
The Guardian Council specified that “all nominees must be between 40 and 70 years of age, hold at least a master’s degree or its equivalent, have experience of at least four years in managerial posts... and have no criminal record”.
The new terms come in implementation of a 2016 directive from Iran’s supreme leader Ali Khamenei for the council to clarify and “determine” the requirements.
The updated requirements are likely to exclude some well-known figures, such as Rouhani’s telecom minister, Mohammad Javad Azari Jahromi, who is 39, or the elite Revolutionary Guards’ Saeed Mohammad, whose rank is below major general.
The increasing number of Revolutionary Guard generals who have announced their candidacy or are likely to be intending to compete in the presidential race, have raised fears of the “militarization” of the political circle within the Iranian regime.
f72d47bc58f8c6835fff2b412c57ce03:
Conservative hardliner Ebrahim Raisi has registered as a candidate in Iran's presidential elections.
Raisi is favored to win the election, potentially complicating talks between President Joe Biden and Iran over its nuclear program.
Raisi has previously criticized the terms of the nuclear deal struck by incumbent Hassan Rouhani.
Raisi has the support of a wide range of conservatives and hardliners, who want to expand Iran's nuclear program.
Raisi's background as a hardline judge has raised concerns among reformists and rights groups.
A survey found that a majority (51 percent) of Iranians approved of the JCPOA, compared with only 44 percent in October 2020.
A clear majority (69 percent) of Iranians said that Iran should not get involved in nuclear talks until the U.S. returns to the JCPOA and fulfills its obligations.
Ali Larijani, a former adviser to the supreme leader, has also signed up for the election on June 18.
Over 59 million people are eligible to vote in the election, but there is expected to be a low turnout due to economic problems, international isolation, and a lack of basic freedoms.
c4e484da0c5f7669240d67f95f5a07f8:
Iran's presidential election will be held on June 18, with two main candidates being ultraconservative Ebrahim Raisi and moderate conservative Ali Larijani.
Larijani, a former parliament speaker and advisor to the supreme leader, submitted his candidacy on the final day of registration.
Raisi, the judiciary chief, announced his candidacy in a statement and appeared at the ministry to sign up.
Larijani criticized Raisi and other candidates with military backgrounds, stating that the economy should not be managed with "shouts and orders."
Larijani emphasized the importance of the economy and accused others of "promising paradise" in the country's current state.
Raisi said he aims to bring about change in the executive management of the country and fight against poverty, corruption, humiliation, and discrimination.
Larijani supports the 2015 nuclear deal and called for "smart relations with the West, strong and constructive relations with the East, and brotherly relations with our neighbours."
The Guardian Council will vet the candidates and publish a list of approved candidates by May 27.
2f1a2e3aa0c40306d59dcbb1ec236d7e:
Iran's election in June will determine the next president and possibly the successor of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
Khamenei, who has been in power since 1989, is 81 years old and has several health problems.
The position of supreme leader is critical for the survival of the Islamic Republic and the continuation of Ayatollah Khomeini's revolutionary concept of Velayat-e Faqih.
The supreme leader has the final say on Iran's domestic and foreign policy and significant control over the legislative, executive and judicial systems.
The supreme leader also controls the IRGC, intelligence service, bonyad charitable trusts, and Setad organization.
The position of president can be a crucial stepping stone to succeeding the supreme leader.
Khamenei has increased his interventions in the presidential election and has even told the grandson of the Islamic Republic's founder, Hassan Khomeini, not to run.
The Guardian Council has significantly narrowed its terms for qualification for the presidential election, barring anyone older than 75 and younger than 40 from running.
The Guardian Council will also probably disqualify figures such as Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and anyone else the supreme leader disapproves of.
c875ebd76808807fa1aeb64174c5cfb4:
Iran’s Guardian Council began reviewing applications for the presidential race slated for June 18.
The Council refused to approve Expediency Council secretary and ex-commander of Revolutionary Guards General Mohsen Rezai.
The Council also refused to approve Gen. Saeed Muhammad, the executive director and second brigadier general in the Revolutionary Guard.
Iranian reformist Mohammed Ali Abtahi said the “tsunami” of filed presidential bids confused all equations, especially conservatives backing Ebrahim Raisi before Saeed Jalili entered the election scene.
Abtahi called for “upholding the constitution” in approving the candidacy of presidential runners from both political currents.
7c3cfb35488c814ae10843975a8b24f9:
Iran's Guardian Council approved seven candidates to run in June's presidential poll, including ultraconservative judiciary chief Ebrahim Raisi.
Former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was not approved to run for another term.
Former parliament speaker Ali Larijani was also barred from running.

Iran approved seven candidates for the presidential poll in June, with ultraconservatives dominating the list.

The final list announcement comes amid ongoing nuclear talks in Vienna.
Larijani, a key supporter of the 2015 nuclear deal, accepted his disqualification.
Analysts believe Raisi is likely to win easily due to the disqualification of his main rivals.
8b4edc27b82bd0b0bbbd19acbab21519:
Supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei urged Iranians to ignore calls to boycott next month’s presidential election.
Iranians are set to elect a successor to President Hassan Rouhani on June 18.
Iran’s candidate-vetting Guardian Council approved seven mainly ultraconservative hopefuls to run in the election and disqualified moderate conservative Ali Larijani and firebrand former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

The poll comes at a critical time for Iran amid talks with world powers aimed at reviving a nuclear deal.
4aa445ec4be711f18aceb1b34b95091a:
Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei supported the disqualification of leading moderate and conservative candidates for the June presidential election by the Guardian Council.
The Guardian Council approved seven out of 592 hopefuls including Iran's hardline judiciary chief Ebrahim Raisi.
Iranian President Hassan Rouhani asked the Supreme Leader to ensure greater "competition" in the elections.
Official opinion polls suggest turnout in the vote could be as low as 30%.

a1a72cc70130e97ee06448a07985207a:
The Guardian Council has barred establishment candidate Ali Larijani from the Iranian presidential race.
Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei defended the Guardian Council's decision to exclude moderates from the presidential election.
President Hassan Rouhani urged a rethink on the matter, emphasizing the importance of competition in elections.

Iran's judiciary chief Ebrahim Raisi's chances of winning the presidency have increased with Larijani's disqualification.

e87034aaa915a2ef011c9d734750b545:
Iran's supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, has decided not to interfere with the Guardian Council's decision to keep the list of presidential candidates intact, guaranteeing the election of a conservative candidate.
Khamenei's decision is seen as a move to ensure that his successor will be a conservative.
The upcoming Iranian presidential elections, to be held on June 18th, will feature only conservative candidates, increasing alienation between the Iranian regime and the population.
Khamenei's decision may be related to concerns that another loss by Ibrahim Raisi, head of Iran's judiciary, would undermine the legitimacy of the conservatives and Khamenei himself.
Khamenei may also be concerned about his weakening abilities to withstand attempts by Rouhani and his men to get closer to the West.

Iran's presidential election system is fundamentally authoritarian, despite claims of democracy.
Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei appoints the IRGC's senior generals and the head of the judiciary, giving the military and judicial apparatuses an undemocratic character.
The Guardian Council, an unelected body appointed by Khamenei, disqualifies reform-minded candidates, women, and those perceived as disloyal to the state, limiting the people's choice in elections.
Khamenei insists Iran's elections are flawless, as he can select the candidates he wants to be president.
For the 2021 presidential election, the Guardian Council disqualified anyone who could have defeated Khamenei's pick, Ebrahim Raisi.

Iran’s Guardian Council will announce a review of candidates barred from this month’s presidential vote following the Supreme Leader’s intervention.
